scope: Theorem 4.8 (The determinant-one two-tower comparison) of the manuscript “Failure of finite assembly for a chromatic overlap at the prime three” (preprints/Failure-of-finite-assembly-for-a-chromatic-overlap-at-the-prime-three-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 318 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 b1e58a49eb364dd8), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 20. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For each open U ⊂ J and B = LU there is a natural equivalence of v-stacks over k [Spa(B♭ )/H] ≃ [N∗ /U]. (4.10) It is obtained from the commuting torsor presentations ˜︁ X/U ≃ Spa(B♭ ), ˜︁ X/H ≃ N∗ . The residual group P/H = Z× p acts on N∗ by kernel scalars through reduced norm, up to the common inverse convention. The J-action changes the quotient frame and makes the kernel determinant adjustment in (4.9). All these identifications commute with base change and products with profinite parameter spaces.
